privacy.metaDescription: How Cognos handles your information. We keep no copy of your chats we can read.
privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.lead: How we handle your information — in plain language, privacy first.

intro.p: Cognos is an encrypted AI chat application by Climacrux GmbH, St. Niklausenstrasse 96, 6047 Kastanienbaum, Switzerland.
We built Cognos for private, useful AI conversations. This policy explains what we collect, what we do with it, and what we deliberately do not do.
For privacy questions, contact us at privacy@cognos.io.

blocks.p: Cognos stores your chat history in an encrypted form.
That means:

ul: Stored chat history is encrypted so Cognos cannot read it from storage.
Live AI requests are processed in plaintext by our backend and the selected AI provider so the AI can answer.
We do not use your chats to train our own models.
We do not sell your personal data.
We do not share your data for advertising.
We require approved AI providers not to use Cognos chats for training.

blocks.p: This is not the same as full end-to-end encryption for the entire AI request path. Your stored history is protected, but when you send a message, that message has to be processed so the AI can respond.

sections.heading: Who is responsible for your data?

blocks.p: The controller is:

Climacrux GmbH
St. Niklausenstrasse 96
6047 Kastanienbaum
Switzerland
Email: privacy@cognos.io
We have not appointed a Data Protection Officer. We have not confirmed an EU or UK representative. This section may be updated after legal review.
Cognos is intended for users aged 16 or older, unless a different age applies under local law or after legal review.
Cognos is available worldwide, with a primary focus on Switzerland, the UK, Germany, France, Spain, Portugal, and Italy.
This policy currently covers the Cognos web app.
We collect the information needed to create, secure, and manage your account, such as:

ul: email address
password hash and authentication data
preferred language, theme, model, and privacy tier
avatar icon and colour
multi-factor authentication status, if enabled
account settings and preferences
billing status and subscription references

blocks.p: Current sign-in is email/password. Google and Apple login may be added later. Authenticator-app MFA is supported. Passkeys are planned.
Your chats may include:

ul: messages and prompts
AI responses
generated content
conversation titles
summaries and memory used to make conversations work better
supported file-derived context
personas and settings
redaction mappings

blocks.p: Stored chat history is encrypted at rest and decrypted client-side. Cognos does not store your Account Key on our servers.
During a live AI request, your message is processed in plaintext by Cognos backend systems and by the selected AI provider so the AI can generate a response.
You may upload supported files such as text, documents, PDFs, DOCX files, images, and code-like text.

Files are processed in the browser where possible for extraction, redaction, and encryption. They are encrypted before upload. File context may be sent to an AI provider when you use that file in a message.
We do not use uploaded files to train models.
We have not found current use of third-party OCR, transcription, malware scanning, or audio upload vendors. If this changes, this policy will be updated.
Payments are handled by Paddle.
Cognos does not store full payment card details. Paddle handles payment cards, tax, checkout, and invoices.
Cognos may store:

ul: Paddle customer and subscription IDs
billing status
invoice metadata
business name
VAT number
billing country
usage ledger data
limited card display details, such as brand, last four digits, or expiry, if provided by Paddle

blocks.p: Billing records are linked to your account, but not to your chat content.
We collect limited operational data to run, secure, and bill for the service, such as:

ul: IP address
user agent
timestamps
routes and request status
error information
model used
provider used
privacy tier
token counts
cost and latency metadata
billing identifiers

blocks.p: We do not intentionally log prompts, completions, message content, or encryption keys.
Approximate region may be inferred from your IP address by infrastructure or analytics providers. We do not collect precise location.
Cognos may use privacy-friendly product analytics, such as Plausible, to understand aggregate product usage.
If enabled, analytics are intended to be cookieless and not to include chat content, prompts, completions, or personal identifiers.
We do not use session replay, heatmaps, keystroke logging, screen recording, or advertising pixels.
We aim to respect Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control signals where applicable.
We process data to:

ul: provide the Cognos chat service
store encrypted chat history
route AI requests to selected models and providers
manage accounts, login, and MFA
process subscriptions and billing
provide support
secure the service
prevent abuse
maintain logs needed for operations and security
improve product reliability and usability
comply with legal, tax, and accounting obligations

blocks.p: Where GDPR-style rules apply, we rely on these legal bases:

ul: Contract: to provide Cognos, manage accounts, process subscriptions, and deliver AI responses.
Legitimate interests: to secure the service, prevent abuse, maintain essential logs, debug issues, and improve the product.
Legal obligation: to keep records required for tax, accounting, and legal compliance.
Consent: where required, for optional marketing or non-essential analytics.

blocks.p: Cognos lets users choose models. Model availability is gated by the user’s selected privacy tier, such as Switzerland-only, EU, or global options.
When you send a message, Cognos routes the request to the selected or eligible AI provider. That provider processes the prompt and response so the AI can answer.
We do not use your chats to train our own models.
We require approved AI providers not to use Cognos user data for training. Exact provider retention terms depend on our contracts and provider configuration.
Current or expected AI infrastructure includes:

ul: Infomaniak for Swiss-hosted models
Requesty as an EU gateway
the underlying model providers and hosts listed on our Subprocessors page

sections.heading: Subprocessors: who helps us run Cognos?

blocks.p: We use a small number of service providers to operate Cognos.
Some help us host the app, send emails, process payments, store encrypted backups, deliver the website, or provide AI responses. They may process personal data only for those purposes.
Important distinction:

ul: hosting and backup providers mainly process encrypted stored data and technical metadata
billing providers process payment and invoice data
email providers process email addresses and email content
AI providers process plaintext prompts and responses during live AI requests so the AI can answer

blocks.p: We do not let service providers sell Cognos user data or use it for advertising.

Some providers process only encrypted data or technical metadata. AI providers are different: they process live prompts and responses in plaintext so the AI can answer. Stored chat history remains encrypted so Cognos cannot read it from storage.
See our full, always-current subprocessor list — who each provider is, what they handle and where — on the Subprocessors page.

We require AI providers used with Cognos not to use Cognos user data for model training. Exact retention and routing terms depend on the provider and selected privacy tier. We use contractual safeguards where required, including data processing agreements and international transfer protections.
Cognos uses client-side encryption for stored chat data.
In practical terms:

ul: stored chat history is encrypted at rest
stored files and attachments are encrypted at rest
conversation titles, summaries, memory, personas, attachment manifests, artifacts, and redaction mappings are encrypted at rest
your Account Key is generated client-side and is not sent to Cognos servers
private keys are encrypted client-side before backup
conversation and file keys are wrapped or sealed for authorised users
live AI requests are processed in plaintext so the AI can answer

blocks.p: We also use security measures such as:

ul: TLS in transit
access controls
route authorisation
MFA support
rate limits
password lockout
hardened containers
firewall controls
backups
operational monitoring

blocks.p: Cognos staff should not be able to read stored chat content from the database. Staff access to production systems is restricted. Staff are not permitted to inspect plaintext live request flows except where strictly necessary and authorised for security or operational reasons.
We maintain incident-response procedures and restrict production access to authorised staff on a need-to-know basis, with access logged and reviewed.
We do not:

ul: sell your personal data
share your personal data for advertising
use your chats to train Cognos models
intentionally log prompts or AI completions
store full payment card details
use advertising pixels
use session replay, heatmaps, or keystroke logging
scan encrypted stored chat history for advertising or profiling

blocks.p: We use service providers to run Cognos. These vendors may process personal data only as needed to provide their services.
Current or planned service providers include:

ul: Hetzner, for app/backend hosting
Bunny.net, for CDN/DNS
BorgBase, for backups
Scaleway, for transactional email
Paddle, for payments, subscriptions, tax, and invoices
Infomaniak, for Swiss AI infrastructure
Requesty, for AI gateway services
Ghost, for marketing site infrastructure
GitHub, for development infrastructure
Grafana Alloy or related tooling, for server monitoring
Plausible, if launched, for cookieless analytics

blocks.p: Some providers may process data outside Switzerland, the EU, or the EEA. Where required, we use appropriate safeguards such as data processing agreements and standard contractual clauses.
Cognos is operated by a Swiss company. Core app/backend hosting is currently on Hetzner infrastructure in Falkenstein, Germany. The frontend may be served through Hetzner and Bunny.net.
Depending on your selected privacy tier, AI provider, billing interactions, email delivery, CDN routing, support, or infrastructure services, your data may be processed in other countries.
Where required, we use contractual and legal safeguards for international transfers.
Cognos uses local storage and similar technologies for essential app functionality and preferences, such as:

ul: language
theme
encrypted vault-session data
authentication state

blocks.p: Paddle may use its own cookies or storage during checkout.
If Plausible analytics is enabled, it is intended to be cookieless.
We do not currently use Google Analytics, PostHog, Meta Pixel, LinkedIn Ads, Sentry, or advertising cookies.
Cognos supports public chat sharing.
If you choose to make a chat public or share it through a public link, people with access to that link may be able to view the shared content. Only share conversations you are comfortable disclosing.
Cognos is designed for private questions, but you should avoid adding unnecessary sensitive personal data, confidential business data, health data, financial data, government IDs, or secrets.
Encryption and redaction reduce exposure, but they do not eliminate all risk. Live AI requests still require plaintext processing by Cognos backend systems and the selected AI provider.
We keep data only as long as needed for the purposes described in this policy.
Current retention approach:

ul: account data is kept while your account exists
chat data is kept until you delete it, it expires, or your account is deleted
deleted ordinary records are snapshotted for 30 days in a deleted-record table
key material and user attachment records are excluded from that 30-day deleted-record snapshot
removed user attachments are hard-deleted
financial records may be detached from your account and retained as required for accounting, tax, or legal purposes
backups follow a rotation of hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, and yearly snapshots
yearly backups may be kept for up to 10 years

blocks.p: Operational logs, support messages, and abuse or security records are kept only as long as needed for security, support, and legal obligations, then deleted or anonymised. Some billing records are kept for longer where accounting, tax, or legal rules require.
You can delete your account, subject to any steps needed to cancel an active paid plan first.
Account deletion removes user-owned:

ul: conversations
messages
keys
projects, where applicable
personas
preferences
vault sessions

blocks.p: Financial records may be retained in detached form where required for legal, tax, accounting, refund, fraud-prevention, or compliance reasons.
Depending on where you live, you may have rights to:

ul: access your personal data
correct inaccurate data
delete your data
export your data
object to certain processing
restrict certain processing
withdraw consent
complain to a data protection authority

blocks.p: Cognos supports browser-side export for conversations and data. You can also delete conversations and manage account settings in the app.
To make a privacy request, email privacy@cognos.io.
We may need to verify your identity before fulfilling a request.
We send transactional emails such as:

ul: account verification
password reset
authentication and security messages
billing and subscription messages
support replies

blocks.p: Marketing emails or newsletters are not currently confirmed. If we send marketing emails, you will be able to opt out.
We may disclose information if legally required.

If we receive a valid legal request for stored chat content, Cognos can only provide the encrypted content and metadata it has. Cognos cannot decrypt stored chat history from storage without the user’s Account Key and relevant keys.
Live AI request processing and metadata are different from encrypted stored history and may be subject to normal operational and legal processes.
Cognos is not intended for children under 16. If you believe a child has used Cognos in violation of this policy, contact us at privacy@cognos.io.
We may update this policy as Cognos changes or as legal requirements evolve.
If changes are material, we will provide reasonable notice, such as through the app or by email.

subprocessors.title: Subprocessors
subprocessors.lead: The short list of trusted providers behind Cognos — what each does, what it may handle, and where.

intro.p: Running Cognos takes a handful of specialist providers — for hosting, backups, account emails, payments, delivering the website and the AI itself. We keep the list short on purpose.
This page names every provider we rely on, what it does and what it may handle. It sits alongside our Privacy Policy, which explains the wider picture.

blocks.p: Not every provider sees the same thing. The important difference is between the ones that only ever handle data in a form we can’t read, and the AI providers that briefly work with your message while they answer.

ul: hosting and backup providers mainly handle stored data that stays locked, plus technical details like timestamps
the payments provider handles payment and invoice details
the email provider handles your email address and the emails we send you
AI providers work with your message and its answer while the AI is responding — the one moment your message is readable, and it’s never kept afterwards

blocks.p: Whatever a provider is doing, your saved chat history always stays locked in storage, in a form Cognos can’t read.

security.metaDescription: How Cognos keeps your chats private: locked in a form we can’t read, opened only by a key you hold, and handled in Switzerland or Europe.
security.title: Security
security.lead: A plain-language look at how Cognos is built, what we can and can’t see, and the limits we’re honest about.

intro.p: Cognos is an AI chat app built so that your saved conversations are kept in a form we can’t read. This page explains how that works, in plain language.
For the precise legal detail, see our Privacy Policy. For the providers behind Cognos, see Subprocessors.

blocks.p: Three parts work together every time you chat, and each is trusted with as little as possible.

ul: Your device holds the keys. Your chats are unlocked and read here, and nowhere else.
Our servers store your chats locked, pass your message to the AI, and lock the answer away again. They never keep a copy we can read.
The AI provider receives your message only while it answers, then keeps nothing.

blocks.p: When a conversation is saved, it’s locked on your device before it reaches us — the messages, titles, summaries and any files. We store only the locked version, which we can’t read.
Only your key can open it again, and that happens on your device when you sign in.
You have two separate secrets, each with one job:

ul: Your password signs you in. Forget it and you can reset it by email — your chats stay safe, because the password doesn’t unlock them.

Your Account Key is the one that opens your chats. We never receive it or store it, so keep it somewhere safe. If you lose it, we can’t recover your chats for you — that’s the trade-off for keeping no copy we can read.

sections.heading: What we can and can’t see

blocks.p: We can see the details needed to run the service — your account and billing information, which model you used, and technical details like timestamps. While the AI is answering, your message is readable so the AI can work with it.
We can’t read your saved chats, titles, summaries, memory or files from storage. They stay locked with a key we don’t hold.

Before your message leaves your device, Cognos also hides common personal details — like emails, phone numbers, bank details and ID numbers — behind placeholders, so the AI works with placeholders instead of the real values.
Cognos is run by a Swiss company. The app and its stored data are hosted in Europe, and you choose whether AI models run in Switzerland only or across Europe.

We keep data only as long as we need it. Your chats stay until you delete them, they expire, or you close your account. Deleted items are held briefly in a recovery snapshot before they’re gone for good, and backups rotate on a regular schedule.
A short list of specialist providers helps us host the app, send emails, take payments and provide the AI. Most only ever handle data in a form we can’t read.
See the full list — who they are, what they handle and where — on the Subprocessors page.
The parts of Cognos that handle your data are open for inspection, so you can verify what we do rather than take our word for it.
Cognos hasn’t yet completed a formal independent security audit. We’ll say so here plainly when that changes.
We’re upfront about the limits:

ul: While the AI answers, your message has to be readable to our systems and the AI provider. This is the one moment it isn’t locked, and it’s never kept afterwards.
Hiding personal details is automatic but best-effort — it catches common things like emails and card numbers, not everything.
If someone reaches your device while it’s unlocked, they can see what you can see. Locking or signing out protects a device you’ve stepped away from.
If you lose your Account Key, your chats can’t be recovered.

blocks.p: Cognos is built to protect your saved chats if our storage or database is ever breached — not to hide your message from the AI while it’s answering.

about.metaDescription: Why Cognos exists, what we hold ourselves to, and the small Swiss team building AI that's private by architecture, not by policy.
about.title: Privacy shouldn't be a setting. It should be the foundation.
about.lead: We build AI that's private by architecture, not by policy — because a promise can be broken and a subpoena can be answered, but maths can't be argued with.

origin.title: The most private thing you own shouldn't live on someone else's server, readable.
body: Every AI assistant sees your unfinished thoughts before anyone else does — your health questions, your finances, the message you're drafting to your boss. Most of that gets kept, readable, indefinitely, on infrastructure you don't control and can't audit.

We didn't think that trade-off was necessary. The idea of keeping no readable copy isn't new — it's how private messaging has worked for over a decade. We built Cognos to bring it to AI: your chats are saved locked, opened only by a key you hold, so the assistant works exactly the same — but there's nothing left for us to leak, sell, or be forced to hand over.
We're based in Switzerland, deliberately — one of the strongest privacy and data-protection regimes anywhere, and a useful forcing function to build things right the first time.
origin.quote: We built it so the only copy we keep is one we can't read. That's not a promise — it's something you can verify.

why.title: The same AI. None of the exposure.
body: Most AI tools keep what your team types — and can read it. That turns every pasted contract, patient note or client email into a risk. Cognos works the other way round: we keep no copy of your team's chats that we can read, and personal details are hidden before a message is even sent.
Everything is handled in Switzerland or Europe, under some of the strongest privacy laws anywhere. When a client asks where their data goes, you have a straight answer.
